newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes slightly down, off lows.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes slightly down, off lows.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed $1 a tonne down on Tuesday having shed earlier gains as NYMEX heating oil weakened.

But the Feb contract bounced off session lows in the last few minutes of trade on a report that United Nations inspectors have discovered that Iraq has continued to develop missiles in contravention of U.N. resolutions.
Feb gas oil closed $1 down at $203 a tonne, $1 up from the intra-day low, but more than $5 off the session high.

In an advance release from Wednesday's edition, the daily Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) said the United States could make a decision this week on whether to launch a Tomahawk missile strike at Iraq. It sourced its report to "American security sources".
IPE Brent also bounced higher on the news, but failed to reclaim all earlier losses. March Brent was trading 12 cents down at $22.42 a barrel at 1744 GMT.
Brent and gas oil earlier came under pressure as NYMEX heating oil fell.
Forecasts for above-normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the world's key heating oil market, undermined oil market on both sides of the Atlantic, dealers said.
Expectations that weekly U.S. inventory data, to be released after the close of trade today may show a climb in distillate stocks on year-ago levels, was also bearish, they said.
"There is talk that this week's APIs will show a positive year-over-year comparison," said a U.S. oil products trader.
